name.en: Fake USPS text: “your package can’t be delivered, update your address”

how.en: A text says it is from USPS and that your package is waiting, couldn’t be delivered, has unpaid postage or needs an address fix. It asks you to tap a link to “fix the problem”. The link opens a look-alike USPS website that asks for your name, address and card number, often for a small fee. USPS only sends tracking texts if you asked for them with a tracking number, and those texts don’t contain links.

text.en: A text claims to be from USPS about a package.
It says delivery failed, postage is unpaid or your address is incomplete.
It asks you to tap a link to fix the problem.
The fake site asks for your personal details and card number, often for a small fee.
USPS: Your package could not be delivered due to an incomplete address. Please update your information within 24 hours or the package will be returned: [link]

en: A delivery text you didn’t sign up for, with a link.
A failed delivery, unpaid postage or a missing address detail.
A deadline before the package is “returned”.
A request for card details or a small fee.
Don’t tap the link. Check tracking by typing the USPS address into your browser, or with the store you ordered from.
Forward the text to 7726 (SPAM), then delete it.
If you tapped the link or entered details, contact your bank or card issuer.
Report USPS texts to the Postal Inspection Service.
